first_impression.reaction: Sophie sent this, so I'll read it properly. I liked "We sell neither." That's the first thing I'd want to know. It's sensible and calm, nobody's trying to be trendy. It's not really my decision though. It's their ring, and I'm paying towards the wedding, not the stone.

journey.quote: We sell neither. This guide separates what is settled (the material, the hardness, the grading and the naming rules) from what is genuinely uncertain, then answers "worth it" as a question of values, with the paperwork to insist on either way.
journey.reaction: Good. Someone who isn't selling me anything, and who mentions paperwork in the second paragraph.

journey.quote: Yes. GIA explains that laboratory-grown diamonds have the same crystal structure as natural diamonds, tightly bonded carbon atoms, which gives them nearly the same chemical, optical and physical properties.
journey.reaction: Honestly, I had assumed they were a sort of fake. This answers that for me, and I can tell Geoff without it turning into an argument.

journey.quote: A capsule holding a carbon source and a mix of metals is heated to about 1300 to 1600°C at pressures of 5 to 6 GPa, the equivalent of 150 to 190 km beneath the Earth's surface.
journey.reaction: More science than I need. I skimmed this bit.

journey.quote: These are US rules, as at October 2026, but they are the clearest naming benchmark the industry has.
journey.reaction: Why am I reading about American rules first? I'd rather have the Australian section higher up. It's fine, but a long way in before I get to what applies here.

journey.quote: In Australia, the ACCC says any claim a business makes about its products must be accurate, truthful and based on reasonable grounds, whether or not it intends to mislead.
journey.reaction: That's the reassurance I wanted. Someone is accountable for what the jeweller tells them.

journey.section: Do lab-grown diamonds hold their value?
journey.quote: Ask the seller about buy-back or upgrade terms, and get them in writing.
journey.reaction: Exactly what I'd tell Sophie. Get it in writing.

journey.section: Heirloom, rarity and what "forever" means to you
journey.quote: You may hear firm opinions on both sides, from jewellers and from family. Neither view makes the other wrong.
journey.reaction: I know that's partly about me. It's said kindly, it doesn't make me feel old-fashioned, and it tells them to have the conversation. I can live with that.

journey.section: The paperwork to insist on either way
journey.quote: Any treatment, buy-back or upgrade terms in writing before you pay.
journey.reaction: A clear checklist I could print out. This is the most useful part for me.

journey.section: From the ring to the destination
journey.quote: When you are ready, your Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments as your one point of contact, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: That's the line I'd underline for Geoff. One person, and the fee agreed in writing. But I'd still want to know who that person is and whether I can ring them.

unanswered_questions: Can I speak to the Wedded Advisor on the phone before anything is booked, and who exactly would that be?
Are deposits paid through you protected if an overseas supplier lets us down?
Are quotes given in Australian dollars?
would_share_with: My husband Geoff, with the paperwork checklist circled
Sophie, to say I've read it

cta_reaction.quote: You can talk to a Wedded Concierge about a proposal or wedding abroad.
cta_reaction.why: Not because of the ring. That's theirs to decide. But the line about one point of contact and the fee in writing has me curious about the wedding side, so I might click to see whether I can get someone on the phone.

top_3_changes: Move 'What Australian Consumer Law expects' above the US FTC section, so the rules that apply to us come first.
Next to the Wedded Advisor line, say plainly that you can speak to someone on the phone before anything is booked.
Trim or box the HPHT/CVD temperature and pressure detail so careful readers aren't wading through science to reach the practical parts.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent, reads carefully, wants a phone call, practical questions)
No invented brand facts; missing details (phone contact, deposit protection, AUD quotes) listed as unanswered questions, and deferred business details not treated as must-fix
HTML comments and fact markers treated as invisible
